messages.subject: How to go around "Rejecting initial value"?
parts:
Hi, All,

I'm trying to model response bias for polytomous Likert-scale, that it the lower asymptote for each thresholds. So I first generated the data with the following core codes:

### Generating Item parameters for n.items ###
# Item discrimination ranges from U(0, 2)
        item.disc <- runif(n.items, 0.5, 2)

# Response Bias
        response.bias <- rbeta(n.items, 5, 27)
      
# Initialze threhold matrix for graded response model with 10 items there are n.categories - 1 thresholds for n.categories
        thresholds <- as.data.frame(matrix(0, n.items, (n.categories - 1)))
      
### Generating latent trait for n.observations ###
# latent traits ranges from N(0, 1)
        theta <- rnorm(n.observations, 0, 1)
      
### Generating the FIRST threshold for 10 items
        thresholds[, 1] <- rnorm(n.items, threshould.First, 1)
      
### Generating the REST thresholds for 10 items
# From thresholds[, 2] to thresholds[, n.categories - 1] has a mean increase of .2
        for(i in 1:n.items)
          {
            for(t in 2:(n.categories-1))
              {
                thresholds[i,t] <- thresholds[i,(t-1)] + runif(1, .5, .9)
              }
          }
            
### Generating response patterns
# initialize the probability of being each categories
        prob <- array(0, c(n.observations, n.items, n.categories)) # probability of being in a specific thresholds
        qrob <- array(0, c(n.observations, n.items, n.categories)) # probability of being in a specific categories
        prob.start <- array(1, c(n.observations, n.items, n.categories)) # probability of being in a specific thresholds
        response.pattern <- as.data.frame(matrix(NA, n.observations, n.items)) # response pattern based on prob
        
        for(i in 1:n.observations)
        {
          for(j in 1:n.items)
          {
            # Draw a random number to determine categories
            start.category <- runif(1, 0, 1)
            
            for (k in 1:(n.categories - 1)) {
              prob.start[i, j, k] <- 1 / (1+ exp(-item.disc[j]*(theta[i]-thresholds[j,k]))) # probability of being in a specific categories, 2PL, either in or out
            }
            
            qrob[i, j, 1] <-  prob.start[i, j, 1] # probability of being in a categories 1
            prob[i, j, 1] <- response.bias[j] + (1-response.bias[j])*qrob[i, j, 1] # the lower asymptote is non-zero for thresholds
            
            for (k in 2:(n.categories - 1)){
              qrob[i, j, k] <- prob.start[i, j, k] - prob.start[i, j, k-1] # probability of being in a categories 2 to n_categories-1
              prob[i, j, k] <- response.bias[j] + (1-response.bias[j])*qrob[i, j, k] # the lower asymptote is non-zero for thresholds
            }
            
            qrob[i, j, n.categories] <- prob.start[i, j, n.categories - 1] # probability of being in categories n_categories
            prob[i, j, n.categories] <- 1-(response.bias[j]+(1-response.bias[j])*qrob[i, j, n.categories]) # the lower asymptote is non-zero for thresholds


### Generating 5 level likert-scale ###
        if(n.categories == 5)
                  {
                    if (start.category <= prob[i, j, 1])
                      {
                        response.pattern[i,j] <- 1
                      } else
                        if (start.category <= prob[i,j,1]+prob[i,j,2])
                          {
                            response.pattern[i,j] <- 2
                          } else
                            if (start.category <= prob[i,j,1]+prob[i,j,2]+prob[i,j,3])
                              {
                                response.pattern[i,j] <- 3
                              } else
                                if (start.category <= prob[i,j,1]+prob[i,j,2]+prob[i,j,3]+prob[i,j,4])
                                  {
                                    response.pattern[i,j] <-4
                                  } else
                                    if (start.category <= 1)
                                      {
                                        response.pattern[i,j] <-5
                                      }
                    names(thresholds) <- c("thresholds.1","thresholds.2","thresholds.3","thresholds.4")
                  }

The code works pretty for me to generate the data, I can get the item cumulative categories curve as I expected.

> Generating[[1]]
      thresholds.1    thresholds.2    thresholds.3    thresholds.4    item.disc     response.bias
 [1,]          0.488               1.005               1.714              2.295          1.793                  0.155

 [3,]         -0.619               0.210               1.020              1.729          1.874                  0.130
 [4,]         -0.459               0.426               1.026              1.698          1.344                  0.147
 [5,]         -1.987              -1.223              -0.392              0.289          0.889                  0.184
 [6,]         -1.611              -0.932              -0.323              0.403          1.747                  0.180
 [7,]          0.140               0.970               1.649              2.217          1.060                   0.178
 [8,]         -1.125              -0.424               0.392              1.234          1.052                   0.172
 [9,]         -0.015               0.622               1.438              1.994           1.284                   0.103
[10,]        -0.710               0.051               0.940              1.447           1.015                   0.125


Then I want to write a stan code to analysis the model, since I know the true model, so I started with using the exact new model to analysis the data.


GRM3PLa <- "

data {

int<lower=0> n_observations; // number of observations

int<lower=0> n_items; // number of items

int<lower=1> n_categories;    // number of categories

int y[n_observations, n_items]; // data

}


parameters {

  real<lower=0, upper=5.5> item_disc[n_items]; // item discriminations

  ordered[n_categories-1] thresholds[n_items]; // item thresholds

  real<lower=0, upper=1> response_bias[n_items]; // item response bias

  real theta[n_observations]; // latent ability

}


model{

  real prob[n_observations, n_items, n_categories];

  real qrob[n_observations, n_items, n_categories];

  real prob_start[n_observations, n_items, n_categories-1];


  item_disc ~ student_t(3, 1, 5); // t distribution

  //item_disc ~ lognormal(0,1);

  theta ~ normal(0,1);

  //response_bias ~ uniform(0, 1);


  for (i in 1: n_items){

    for (j in 1:(n_categories-1)){ 

      thresholds[i,j] ~ normal(0,5);

    }

  }


  for (i in 1:n_observations) {

    for (j in 1:n_items) {

      for (k in 1:(n_categories - 1)) {

        prob_start[i, j, k] <- 1 / (1+ exp(-item_disc[j]*(theta[i]-thresholds[j,k])));

      }


      qrob[i, j, 1] <-  prob_start[i, j, 1];

      prob[i, j, 1] <- response_bias[j] + (1-response_bias[j])*qrob[i, j, 1];


      for (k in 2:(n_categories - 1)){

        qrob[i, j, k] <- prob_start[i, j, k] - prob_start[i, j, k-1];

        prob[i, j, k] <- response_bias[j] + (1-response_bias[j])*qrob[i, j, k];

      }


      qrob[i, j, n_categories] <- prob_start[i, j, n_categories - 1];

      prob[i, j, n_categories] <- 1-response_bias[j]+(1-response_bias[j])*(qrob[i, j, n_categories]);


      // incement log probability directly because Y[i, j]

      // has categorical distribution with varying dimension

        increment_log_prob(log(prob[i, j, y[i, j]]));

    }

  }

}

"


Then I encounter the following error message:

Rejecting initial value:
  Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity.
  Stan can't start sampling from this initial value.
...

Initialization between (-2, 2) failed after 100 attempts. 
 Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model.
[1] "Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) : Initialization failed."
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done.

This error happens with some probability, some chains will be initiated, but some are not.

Can any one give me some idea or cue why this error occurs? Any help will be appreciated, thanks!

Sincerely,

Jiaqi

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to go around "Rejecting initial value"?
parts:
You get rejection when the random inits don't have support in
the model. That's usually because there are missing constraints
in parameter declarations or illegal math or missing definitions.

I'd recommend starting simpler and building up to a more complex
model.

The syntax is now

target += lp;

rather than

increment_log_prob(lp);

- Bob
